response.description: A long and narrow elevation with steep sides.
response.label: ridge

response.description: The raised fault block bounded by normal faults. The raised block is a portion of the Earth's crust that has remained stationary while the land has sunk on either side of it or has been crushed by a mountain range against it.
response.label: horst

response.description: A comparatively elevated area on an icecap.
response.label: ice cap dome

response.description: A section of the Earths's crust that is demarcated by faults or flexures. In the movement of the crust, a massif tends to retain its internal structure while being displaced as a whole.
response.label: massif

response.description: Built by fragments (called ejecta) thrown up (ejected) from a volcanic vent, piling up around the vent in the shape of a cone with a central crater.
response.label: volcanic cone

response.description: An elevated area such as a hill, ridge or old lava dome inside or downslope from an area of active volcanism. New lava flows will cover the surrounding land, isolating the kipuka so that it appears as a (usually) forested island in a barren lava flow.
response.label: kipuka

response.description: Pingos may occur in cold-climate wetland areas, but are not necessarily wetlands themselves.
response.label: pingo

response.description: A geological landform consisting of a steep and often vertical column or columns of rock in the sea near a coast.
response.label: stack

response.description: This is not placed under surface landform, as seamounts are also mounts and are submerged.
response.label: mount

response.description: A tall, slender, spire-shaped rock projecting from a level or more gently sloping surface.
response.label: pinnacle
